citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
During inspection at 12:21PM of an enclosure housing six 7-week old beagle puppies, multiple abnormal fecal
consistencies were noted. The enclosure contained stool with texture but no defined shape as well as watery fecal
material pooled in flat puddles. When questioned, the animal care attendant reported that at approximately 8:10 AM she
observed one puppy producing soft formed to liquid stool during morning cleaning. She stated she did not recall which
puppy was affected and did not notify the attending veterinarian of the abnormal finding. As we continued to observe the
enclosure, one of the puppies defecated, producing stool that was liquid in consistency. Although the attendant
recognized the presence of abnormal fecal material, the failure to communicate this change in health status to the
attending veterinarian delays appropriate assessment and treatment. Such delays can result in preventable pain, distress
or worsening clinical signs in the affected animals. The research facility must establish and maintain a mechanism of
direct and frequent communication so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and
well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian. Corrected at the time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
